int.title: How to_string works for integers
int.description: Writes the number as decimal text.

slides.caption: to_string uses the Display formatting: plain decimal digits, with a minus sign if negative.
The _ in 1_000 is only for reading the source code: "1000".
For padding or hex use format!: format!("{:05}", 42) is "00042", format!("{:x}", 255) is "ff".

float.title: How to_string works for floats
float.description: Writes the shortest text that reads back as the same float.

slides.caption: Display drops a trailing .0 and shows every digit needed to be exact.
0.1 + 0.2 is not exactly 0.3 in binary, and it shows.
Round for people: format!("{:.2}", x) gives two decimals.
The String holds the character's UTF-8 bytes: 1 byte for a, 4 for the crab.
String::from(c) does the same. To add a char to an existing String, use push.

str.title: How to_string works for &str
str.description: Copies borrowed text into a new, owned String.

slides.caption: A &str only borrows its text. to_string makes a String that owns a copy.
The bytes h, e, l, l, o are copied...
...into a new heap buffer the String owns.
String::from("hello") and "hello".to_owned() do exactly the same.

write_str.title: How Formatter::write_str works
write_str.description: Writes plain text from inside a Display or Debug implementation.

title.text: fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter) -> fmt::Result { f.write_str("on") }

slides.caption: write_str sends text to whatever is being formatted into.

pad.title: How Formatter::pad works
pad.description: Writes text while honouring width, alignment and precision flags.

slides.caption: With write_str, {:>6} would be ignored; pad applies it.
Precision .2 cuts the text to 2 chars.
Use pad for text-like types so they line up in tables.

debug_struct.title: How Formatter::debug_struct works
debug_struct.description: Builds Debug output in the Name { field: value } style.

slides.caption: Same output as #[derive(Debug)], but you choose which fields to show.
Skip secrets: leave a password field out of Debug.

debug_tuple.title: How Formatter::debug_tuple works
debug_tuple.description: Builds Debug output in the Name(a, b) style.

debug_list.title: How Formatter::debug_list works
debug_list.description: Builds Debug output in the [a, b, c] style.

slides.caption: Make your own container print like a Vec.

debug_map.title: How Formatter::debug_map works
debug_map.description: Builds Debug output in the {key: value} style.

slides.caption: Each key and value is added.
Use key() and value() for one entry at a time.

alternate.title: How Formatter::alternate works
alternate.description: true if the caller used the # flag ({:#} or {:#?}).

slides.caption: Your Display can offer a second, more detailed form.
derive(Debug) uses it for pretty multi-line output.

precision.title: How Formatter::precision works
precision.description: The precision the caller asked for ({:.2}), if any.

slides.caption: Your type can round itself the way the caller requested.

width.title: How Formatter::width works
width.description: The minimum width the caller asked for ({:8}), if any.

slides.caption: Read it to implement your own alignment.
pad() applies width for you in the common case.

field.title: How DebugStruct::field works
field.description: Adds one name: value pair to a debug_struct output.

slides.caption: Each call appends a field; finish() closes the braces.

finish_non_exhaustive.title: How DebugStruct::finish_non_exhaustive works
finish_non_exhaustive.description: Ends the struct output with .. to show that some fields are hidden.

slides.caption: Readers can see that more fields exist.
Good practice for types holding passwords or tokens.

entry.title: How DebugList::entry works
entry.description: Adds one item to a debug_list output.

entries.title: How DebugList::entries works
entries.description: Adds every item of an iterator to a debug_list output.

finish.title: How DebugList::finish works
finish.description: Closes the list and returns the result.

debug_list-finish_non_exhaustive.title: How DebugList::finish_non_exhaustive works
debug_list-finish_non_exhaustive.description: Closes the list with .. to show more items exist.

debug_map-entry.title: How DebugMap::entry works
debug_map-entry.description: Adds one key: value pair to a debug_map output.

slides.caption: Keys and values are formatted with Debug.
key and value can also be added separately.

debug_map-entries.title: How DebugMap::entries works
debug_map-entries.description: Adds every (key, value) pair of an iterator.

key.title: How DebugMap::key works
key.description: Adds just the key of the next entry; value() must follow.

slides.caption: Useful when the value is computed after the key.
Calling key twice in a row panics.

value.title: How DebugMap::value works
value.description: Adds the value for the key written just before.

slides.caption: Panics if a key was written without its value.

debug_map-finish_non_exhaustive.title: How DebugMap::finish_non_exhaustive works
debug_map-finish_non_exhaustive.description: Closes the map with .. for hidden entries.

slides.caption: Signals that the output is incomplete.
Same idea as for structs and lists.

debug_set.title: How Formatter::debug_set works
debug_set.description: Builds Debug output in the {a, b} style.

debug_set-entry.title: How DebugSet::entry works
debug_set-entry.description: Adds one item to a debug_set output.

debug_set-entries.title: How DebugSet::entries works
debug_set-entries.description: Adds every item of an iterator to a debug_set output.

debug_set-finish_non_exhaustive.title: How DebugSet::finish_non_exhaustive works
debug_set-finish_non_exhaustive.description: Closes the set with .. for hidden items.

slides.caption: With no fields, only the name is printed.

debug_tuple-field.title: How DebugTuple::field works
debug_tuple-field.description: Adds one value to a Name(a, b) output.

slides.caption: Each call adds the next value.
For tuple structs and enum variants.
With no fields it prints only the name.

debug_tuple-finish_non_exhaustive.title: How DebugTuple::finish_non_exhaustive works
debug_tuple-finish_non_exhaustive.description: Closes the tuple output with .. for hidden fields.

slides.caption: Good for types holding keys or tokens.

fill.title: How Formatter::fill works
fill.description: The padding character the caller asked for ({:*>5}).

slides.caption: Read it to pad your own output the same way.
pad() applies fill and width for you.

align.title: How Formatter::align works
align.description: The alignment the caller asked for: Left, Right or Center.

slides.caption: None when no alignment was given.
Numbers then show + for positive values.

sign_minus.title: How Formatter::sign_minus works
sign_minus.description: true if the caller used the - flag ({:-}).

slides.caption: The - flag is accepted but std types ignore it.
Your own types may give it a meaning.

sign_aware_zero_pad.title: How Formatter::sign_aware_zero_pad works
sign_aware_zero_pad.description: true if the caller used 0 padding ({:05}).

pad_integral.title: How Formatter::pad_integral works
pad_integral.description: Writes number digits with sign, prefix, width and zero-padding handled.

slides.caption: You pass sign, prefix and digits; it applies all the flags.
Used by big-number crates to format like built-in ints.

write_fmt.title: How Formatter::write_fmt works
write_fmt.description: What write!(f, ...) calls: writes formatted text into the Formatter.

slides.caption: You normally use the write! macro.
Works for any type implementing fmt::Write too.

write.title: How fmt::write works
write.description: Writes formatted text into any fmt::Write target.

as_str.title: How fmt::Arguments::as_str works
as_str.description: The text as a &str, if it has no {} placeholders to fill.

slides.caption: Loggers use it to skip formatting for constant messages.
It may also return None for plain text in some cases.

from_fn.title: How fmt::from_fn works
from_fn.description: Turns a closure into something you can print with {} or {:?}.

slides.caption: No struct or impl Display needed.
Handy for lazily formatted log fields.

num_buffer_new.title: How NumBuffer::new works
num_buffer_new.description: A stack buffer big enough to format any integer of a type.

slides.caption: Avoids heap allocation for number formatting.

format_into.title: How format_into works on integers
format_into.description: Formats an integer into a stack buffer and returns the text.

i128_format_into.title: How i128::format_into works
i128_format_into.description: Formats an i128 into a stack buffer.

slides.caption: The buffer is sized for the longest value.

u128_format_into.title: How u128::format_into works
u128_format_into.description: Formats a u128 into a stack buffer.

slides.caption: Same idea as for smaller ints.
